subject: Biology
title: Cell: The Unit of Life
summary: Cell theory (Schleiden and Schwann; modified by Rudolf Virchow — omnis cellula e cellula) says all living organisms are made of cells, and all cells arise from pre-existing cells.
Prokaryotic cells (bacteria, cyanobacteria, mycoplasma) lack a nuclear membrane and membrane-bound organelles; eukaryotic cells have both.

The plasma membrane follows the fluid mosaic model (Singer and Nicolson, 1972). The endomembrane system — ER, Golgi, lysosomes, vacuoles — works together; mitochondria and plastids are semi-autonomous with their own DNA and 70S ribosomes.
The nucleus controls the cell; chromosomes are classified by centromere position.

formulas.name: Cell theory
formulas.formula: Schleiden (1838, plants) + Schwann (1839, animals);  Virchow (1855): omnis cellula e cellula

formulas.name: Cell size extremes
formulas.formula: smallest: mycoplasma (~0.3 μm);  bacteria 3–5 μm;  largest single cell: ostrich egg;  human RBC ~7 μm;  longest: nerve cells

formulas.name: Ribosomes
formulas.formula: prokaryotes: 70S (50S + 30S);  eukaryotic cytoplasm: 80S (60S + 40S);  mitochondria and chloroplasts: 70S
formulas.mistake: S (Svedberg unit) measures sedimentation rate, so subunit values don't add up arithmetically.

formulas.name: Fluid mosaic model
formulas.formula: quasi-fluid lipid bilayer with proteins (peripheral and integral);  human RBC membrane ~52% protein, 40% lipid

formulas.name: Membrane transport
formulas.formula: passive (along concentration gradient, no energy — diffusion, osmosis);  active (against gradient, uses ATP — Na⁺/K⁺ pump)

formulas.name: Endomembrane system
formulas.formula: ER + Golgi complex + lysosomes + vacuoles (functions coordinated);  mitochondria, chloroplasts and peroxisomes are NOT part of it

formulas.name: ER functions
formulas.formula: RER (with ribosomes): protein synthesis and secretion;  SER: lipid synthesis; in animals lipid-like steroid hormones are made in SER

formulas.name: Golgi apparatus
formulas.formula: cis (forming, convex) face receives ER vesicles → materials modified → trans (maturing, concave) face releases them to intracellular targets or for secretion outside the cell;  packaging of materials, site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids

formulas.name: Mitochondria
formulas.formula: double membrane, inner folded into cristae; matrix has circular DNA, RNA, 70S ribosomes; site of aerobic respiration (powerhouse); divide by fission

formulas.name: Plastids
formulas.formula: chloroplasts (chlorophyll, carotenoids);  chromoplasts (fat-soluble carotenoids — yellow, orange, red);  leucoplasts: amyloplasts (starch), elaioplasts (oils, fats), aleuroplasts (proteins)

formulas.name: Chloroplast structure
formulas.formula: double membrane; stroma (enzymes, circular DNA, 70S ribosomes); thylakoids stacked as grana; stroma lamellae connect grana

formulas.name: Cilia and flagella
formulas.formula: cilia: short, oar-like — move the cell or the surrounding fluid;  flagella: longer — cell movement;  axoneme with 9 + 2 microtubule arrangement;  centriole and basal body: 9 + 0 (nine triplets, cartwheel)

formulas.name: Chromosome types (by centromere)
formulas.formula: metacentric (middle, equal arms);  sub-metacentric (slightly away);  acrocentric (near end, very short arm);  telocentric (terminal);  centromere (primary constriction) holds the sister chromatids and bears disc-shaped kinetochores that attach spindle fibres in cell division

formulas.name: Nucleus
formulas.formula: double nuclear envelope with pores; nucleoplasm, nucleolus (site of rRNA synthesis) and chromatin (DNA + histones);  interphase nucleus shows chromatin, not chromosomes

examples.title: Semi-autonomous organelles
examples.problem: Which organelles are called semi-autonomous, and why?
examples.solution: Mitochondria and chloroplasts: they have their own circular DNA, RNA and 70S ribosomes, and can make some of their own proteins and divide by fission.

examples.title: Plant vs animal cell
examples.problem: List features present in plant cells but absent in animal cells.
examples.solution: Cell wall, plastids and a large central vacuole. Animal cells have centrioles, which most plant cells lack.

examples.title: Mesosome
examples.problem: What is a mesosome and what does it do?
examples.solution: An infolding of the plasma membrane in bacteria; it helps in cell wall formation, DNA replication and distribution to daughter cells, respiration and secretion, and increases the membrane surface area.

examples.title: Suicidal bags
examples.problem: Why are lysosomes called suicidal bags?
examples.solution: They are filled with hydrolytic enzymes (lipases, proteases, carbohydrases) active at acidic pH; if the membrane bursts the enzymes digest the cell itself.

examples.title: Satellite chromosome
examples.problem: What is a satellite on a chromosome?
examples.solution: A small fragment beyond a secondary constriction — the region that does not stain as darkly; chromosomes with it are called satellite chromosomes.

examples.title: Gram staining
examples.problem: How do Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria differ in staining?
examples.solution: Gram-positive bacteria keep the Gram stain (thick peptidoglycan wall); Gram-negative bacteria do not (thin wall with an outer membrane).

topics.title: Prokaryotic cell envelope
topics.explain: Glycocalyx (slime layer or capsule), cell wall and plasma membrane. Prokaryotes have a nucleoid (naked circular DNA) and often plasmids (small circular DNA giving traits like antibiotic resistance). Inclusion bodies store reserve material: phosphate granules, cyanophycean granules, glycogen; gas vacuoles in some.

topics.title: Bacterial appendages
topics.explain: Flagella (filament, hook, basal body) for movement; pili (elongated tubes) and fimbriae (small bristles, help attachment to rocks or host tissue).

topics.title: Cell wall in plants
topics.explain: Algae: cellulose, galactans, mannans and calcium carbonate. Plants: primary wall (growing cells), secondary wall (inside primary); middle lamella of calcium pectate holds neighbouring cells together; plasmodesmata connect cytoplasm.

topics.title: Vacuoles
topics.explain: Bounded by the tonoplast; in plants can occupy up to 90% of the cell volume and concentrate ions much above the cytoplasm. Contractile vacuoles help osmoregulation in Amoeba; food vacuoles form by engulfing food.

topics.title: Cytoskeleton
topics.explain: Microtubules, microfilaments and intermediate filaments give mechanical support, motility and help maintain cell shape.

topics.title: Centrosome
topics.explain: Usually two cylindrical centrioles at right angles; centrioles form the basal bodies of cilia and flagella and the spindle fibres of the spindle apparatus in animal cell division.

topics.title: Microbodies
topics.explain: Small membrane-bound vesicles containing enzymes, found in both plant and animal cells (peroxisomes, glyoxysomes).

ratta: Endomembrane: ER, Golgi, lysosome, vacuole (not mito/plastid).
Amyloplast starch, elaioplast oil, aleuroplast protein.
Metacentric middle, acrocentric near end, telocentric tip.
Golgi: ER vesicles fuse with cis face;  products leave from trans face.
Centromere → cell division (kinetochores);  cilium → movement;  cristae → mitochondrion.
